title: Antivirus alert on a user PC
symptom: The antivirus has shown a threat alert on a user's PC
user_description: A red box popped up saying a threat was found in something I downloaded. It has a button that says Allow. The file is just a form from a website, can I click Allow?

options.text: Click Allow because she trusts the file
options.why: The antivirus flagged it for a reason. Allowing it could let malware run.

options.text: Turn off the antivirus to stop the pop-ups
options.why: Leaves the PC unprotected exactly when it may be under attack.

options.text: Ignore it since the antivirus probably dealt with it
options.why: You need to check whether it was really quarantined, and the security team needs to know.

options.text: Do not let her dismiss it. Read the alert: was the file quarantined or is it still active? If active or unclear, disconnect the PC from the network, then escalate
options.why: The alert details show how serious it is. Cutting the network contains anything still active, and the security team decides what happens next.

hints: What does the alert itself tell you?
What if the threat is still active?
Who should know about threats found on company PCs?
real_world_tip: Take a photo of the alert before anything closes it. The exact threat name and file path help the security team a lot.

escalation.team_why: Threats on company PCs are handled by the security team. They check whether it spread and whether others downloaded the same file.

details.text: The threat name shown in the alert
details.why: Tells them what kind of malware it is.

details.text: The file path and the time of the alert
details.why: Lets them find the file and the event in their tools.

details.text: Whether it was quarantined or is still active
What she was doing when it appeared (downloading a form from a website)
details.why: Helps them find the source and warn others.

details.text: Her password, so they can sign in and check
details.why: Never share passwords. The security team has its own access.
